messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: Tidy format
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,
I ran into a new error that perhaps you can help remedy, it has to do with a limit of C.

Error in markerforwsel(g, y, n.marcovar) :
  long vectors (argument 3) are not supported in .C
Calls: cim -> markerforwsel
Execution halted

A couple of workarounds i was thinking was thinning my markers to 1/cM, or running per chromosome but i was wondering if you had another solution or knew how to fix this at the C level

Thanks,
Dominick

Im using CIM and ive run a variety of window sizes from 5-100cM, im currently running bootstraps just for comparison, and I am planning on calculating bayesian confidence intervals. My LODs are quite high so LOD drop does not always result in a realistic estimate wider than a single cM location. besides just calling the causative location, i'd also like a better way of comparing between phenotypes if the locations are the same besides just overlaying the plots on one another, any suggestions to this end?

messages.subject: Add'l QTL Effects
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl and r/qtl community,

Just to clarify the process for additional QTL identification and effect estimation, in the presence of multiple QTL.

An outcrossing F1 population was generated and multiple QTL were associated with a trait. Those QTL were made into a qtl object and effects were estimated.

However, additional QTL identification was warranted and a subsequent peak was determined to have a high LOD. It's unclear whether a new permutation threshold should be established, however following the addition to the previous QTL model to estimate effects of the newly-identified QTL, the model is unable to estimate effects.

The data was previously parsed from a larger dataset to include only individuals with a phenotype were used for QTL analyses.

Cheers,
Josh
